content.text:
Silhouette: Four-legged horse frame. Host frame: the horse sets the outline, body size, and overall frame. A single creature that combines a common octopus and a horse. The head is of the horse, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: horse body and legs, with its own dense fur on the face, neck, shoulders, hips, legs, and tail; plain coat, no stripes or spots. From the common octopus, as parts and materials on the horse's own body: soft, color-changing skin with fine bumps in its own colors, grown from the skin as the horse's own covering over the back, flanks, and belly; it replaces the horse's dense fur there and conforms to the horse's body, sized to the horse's body and following its contours. Every covered part keeps the horse's own length and shape; the dense fur stops at the covering's edge, and the face, neck, shoulders, hips, legs, and tail keep the horse's own dense fur. The covering follows the body's own shape. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (rocky coast): dark back and light belly (strong countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws, and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Designing hybrid creature concept**
I'm planning a single creature with a horse silhouette and head, adding octopus skin with fine bumps and color-changing texture over the back, flanks, and belly while keeping dense fur on the face, neck, shoulders, hips, legs, and tail.
**Drafting natural history illustration**
I'm composing a side three-quarter view natural history illustration, keeping horse fur on the head, neck, limbs and tail while covering the back, flanks and belly with soft, color-changing octopus skin with fine bumps and countershading.
